title: SRE oncall scratchpad - 2026-03-22
content:
Quick log + follow-ups from oncall shift (2026-03-22)

-- Morning checks (hand-off notes) 07:30 UTC
- No immediate P0s at handover; briefed by Noah. Main watch: elevated 5xx from hosted-api-route /v1/generate (spike at 03:36-03:52 UTC).
- Noted two elevated errors in telemetry: model-worker OOMs on pool-dedicated-us-east-1-gpu-2 and a downstream Redis auth flake.

-- Incident SRE-1427 (paged 03:36 UTC)
- Page: latency/5xx spike impacting hosted-api customers (approx 12% of requests).
- Pager path: alert from dataplane + increased 5xx rate in API gateway.
- Quick mitigation: scaled up pool-dedicated-us-east-1-gpu-2 by +2 nodes (manual) at 03:40 UTC - reduced tail lat and errors but not fully resolved.
- Observations:
  * model-worker logs show repeated `CudaOutOfMemoryError` for long-context jobs (max_seq_length 4096) - majority from Customer A request pattern.
  * redis-auth errors (~0.5% of API calls) around 03:38-03:45 may have contributed to request retries and load amplification.
- Actions taken during incident:
  1) Throttle set on route /v1/generate at API gateway at 03:42 UTC to protect downstream. (temp throttling)
  2) Began rolling restart of model-worker pods on pool-dedicated-us-east-1-gpu-2 to clear KV cache at 03:44 UTC.
  3) Tagged suspect customer requests - reached out to SE to ask customer to reduce batch size for long-context jobs.
- Incident end (stabilized) 03:52 UTC; monitoring continued until 04:40 UTC.

-- Post-incident notes and follow-ups (to include in follow-up ticket / internal blameless notes)
- Root cause hypothesis: a combination of long-context customer jobs triggering OOMs and a transient Redis auth flake causing retries -> amplified load on GPU pool. Need to verify by correlating retry rates and OOM timestamps.
- Immediate follow-ups (assign and track):
  * SRE-1431: Correlate GPU OOM logs with customer request ids and retry traces - owner: Lena Garcia - due 2026-03-24. (priority: high)
  * SRE-1432: Investigate Redis auth flake root cause (token refresh path, connection pool exhaustion) - owner: Noah Chen - due 2026-03-25. (priority: high)
  * SRE-1433: Update runbook for model-worker OOMs: add recommended auto-scaling thresholds and safe restart procedure to avoid cache stampede - owner: Emily Zhou - draft due 2026-03-23. (priority: medium)
  * Customer outreach: Coordinate with Solutions Eng to ask Customer A to reduce max_seq_length and batch_size for next 24h while we validate - owner: Lucas Morgan - due 2026-03-22 (today).

-- Runbook TODOs (quick notes, flesh out later)
- Add a checklist section for "GPU OOM storm" including: detect OOM rate threshold, safe drain pattern (staggered restarts), temporary throttling rules at API gateway, and quick contact list (SE + account manager).
- Add play for "cache stampede protection": random jittered restarts and temporary prefix caching TTLs.
- Document commands used today (for fast reference):
  * kubectl -n inference get pods -l pool=dedicated-us-east-1-gpu-2
  * kubectl -n inference logs <model-worker-pod> --follow | grep -i oom
  * redis-cli -h redis-prod-1 AUTH <service-token>; monitor slowlog
  * api-gateway CLI: gateway throttle set --route /v1/generate --rate 80rps --burst 100

-- Paging notes (meta)
- Pager response flow worked but need clearer on-call ownership for cross-team escalations (infra vs serving runtime). Create SLAs in runbook for when to escalate to serving-runtime team (e.g., 10+ OOMs in 5m).
- Paging noise: consider adjusting alert thresholds for short-lived spikes that are mitigated by autoscaling within 5m. (Low priority; discussion with observability team)

-- Misc smaller items observed during shift
- Observability: the tracing for retried requests currently loses original request id after two hops - add preservation to trace header (linked: Confluence runbook).
- Cost/ops: check autoscaler cooldown window - currently 3m; might be too short for model cold-starts leading to OOM retries. Add to SRE-1434 (Emily) to evaluate.

-- Personal TODOs (short-term)
- Draft runbook changes for OOM storm (SRE-1433) - due tomorrow.
- Write short email to infra-team about redis token rotation schedule and observed auth-error window.
- Follow up with Solutions Eng re: customer outreach and whether they asked Customer A to throttle.

-- Notes to self (things to remember)
- When scaling pool, monitor KV-cache-hit rate and model cold-start latencies for at least 20m post-scale.
- Use canary restarts (staggered) to avoid simultaneous KV cache eviction across pods.
- Capture full flamegraphs for one of the affected pods and attach to SRE-1431.

End of shift notes. Keep short list in the ticket comments.

Raw incident timeline (timestamps UTC):
- 03:36 alert fired (api-gateway 5xx spike)
- 03:38 investigate & identify OOMs + redis errors
- 03:40 scaled pool + notified SE
- 03:42 applied temporary throttle on /v1/generate
- 03:44 started rolling restarts of model-worker pods (staggered)
- 03:52 5xx rate dropped to baseline; monitoring until 04:40

-- Useful links (copy into ticket)
- Logs view: https://redwood-logs.company/sre/SRE-1427
- Grafana dashboard: https://grafana.company/d/hosted-api/latency-and-errors
- Confluence runbook draft: https://confluence.company/display/SRE/PGM-caching-runbook
- Customer A contact (SE): se-team@example.com
